Landing Page Fit

All traffic runs to a single landing page: directmeds.com/dm-directmax. Its hero leads with aggressive performance/pleasure hype ("Unleash the best sex of your life"), a heavy stack of explicit user testimonials, the 3-in-1 formula (Sildenafil + Tadalafil + Apomorphine), "effects in 15 minutes," and discreet delivery — but shows no actual dollar price anywhere on the page itself, only "33% off." Every ad's creative either reinforces this tone and these specific claims, or clashes with them — and that match (or mismatch) lines up closely with which ads actually convert.
Strong 1 ad · message matches the landing page almost exactly
dm4
"3-in-1 formula," "fast-dissolve," "physician-prescribed online," and "discreet shipping" — the ad's four bullet points are the same four claims the landing page leads with. This is very likely a real contributor to why it's the only ad that converts: there's zero disconnect between what was promised and what's delivered on click-through.
Moderate 6 ads · partial overlap, but a gap somewhere in tone, format, or specificity
dm1
Tone matches (both aggressive/hyperbolic), but the specific "vein popping" claim isn't reinforced on the page, and sits awkwardly next to the LP's doctor-reviewed, LegitScript-approved framing.
dm2
"Delivered" angle echoes the LP's discreet-shipping mentions, but the ad's specific $7.45/dose price is never shown on the page — only a generic "33% off."
dm6
The page does lean on testimonials, so the UGC format isn't wrong — but the hero jumps straight into performance hype rather than continuing the relationship-vulnerability angle the video opens with.
dm8 / dm9
Direct-to-camera format loosely echoes the testimonial section, but the page only has text testimonials — no video — and neither ad's "Special Spark" branding appears anywhere on the page.
New Sales Ad
Generic messaging that doesn't strongly reinforce or conflict with the page — the conversion gap here is more likely page mechanics (load speed, mobile rendering) than a message mismatch.
Weak 2 ads · real tonal or factual mismatch with the page
dm3
A soft, editorial "doctors quietly recommending" tone lands on an aggressive, testimonial-heavy hard-sell page — a jarring shift the moment someone actually clicks through.
dm5
Anchors hard on a specific $79 price point that the landing page never confirms anywhere — undermining the ad's entire "here's the exact deal" pitch the instant someone lands.
dm7
The comedic, playful tone has nowhere to land on a page that's entirely serious hard-sell copy. The joke the ad sets up is never paid off, which likely contributes to its huge reach converting at zero.

Creative Taxonomy vs. Performance

Small-sample caveat: this is 9 ads total, and several taxonomy categories (Convenience, Price_Value, Medical_Credibility) only have one ad each — not enough data to draw a real conclusion about that category alone. The two patterns below are the ones actually supported by more than one data point.
Format: Static 1-for-5, Video 0-for-4.
dm4 (Static) is the only ad with a positive ROAS. All four video ads — regardless of angle, style, or talent — converted at zero. This lines up with the earlier finding that video ads pull cheap, high-CTR attention without buying intent. Directionally consistent, but N=9 is small enough that this should inform testing priorities, not be treated as proof video doesn't work for this offer.
CTA presence: mixed signal, not conclusive.
dm4 (wins) has an explicit "See If You Qualify" CTA; dm1, dm2, and dm5 (all lose) have none. But dm3 also has a CTA and still lost — though dm3's failure is more plausibly explained by its advertorial tone clashing with the landing page (see Landing Page Fit above) and its tiny 3-click sample, not the CTA itself. Worth testing a clear CTA on the currently CTA-less static ads, but don't treat this as settled.
Other observations, noted but not actionable yet (single data point each):
  1. Angle alone doesn't predict the outcome. dm1 and dm4 share the same "Performance" angle — one loses badly (-72.9%), the other is the account's only winner (+155.5%). The difference looks more like tone (graphic/aggressive vs measured/factual) and CTA presence than the angle itself.
  2. "Emotional" style is 0-for-3 (dm6, dm8, dm9) — all lose. Every one of these is also a video, so this may just be re-stating the format finding rather than an independent signal.
  3. Target Age Middle_Aged_35_54 is 1-for-1 — only dm4 sits in this bucket, and it's the winner. Worth deliberately testing this age bracket on other creative angles before reading too much into it.

What to change on the landing page

Add:
  1. Show an actual price (e.g. "$7.45/dose" or "$79/box") somewhere above the fold — right now the page only ever says "33% off" with no dollar figure until deep in the questionnaire flow, which undercuts every price-anchored ad (dm2, dm5).
  2. Add one shorter, lower-key testimonial or a brief note near the hero for ads with a softer or funnier entry point (dm6, dm7) — right now there's an abrupt jump from "relatable/funny" straight into "best sex of your life" with nothing in between.
  3. Add a small trust/credibility element (e.g. the LegitScript badge or "doctor-reviewed" note) higher up on the page, closer to the top — this would help bridge the gap for softer, editorial-style ads like dm3.
Consider removing or toning down:
  1. The most explicit/casual-hookup-framed testimonials (references to multiple partners, "sex god," teenage kids finding the product). Your actual converting audience skews 55+ and male — a page saturated with young-casual-hookup framing may be actively working against the demo that's proven to buy, independent of any ad-creative issue.
  2. The gap between "Order Now" and seeing a real price. Every extra step before showing a dollar amount is a chance to lose someone who clicked an ad that already promised a specific number.

Not yet spending

This data pull only includes the 22 ads that show real activity — unlike earlier exports, it doesn't carry a list of dormant/zero-spend placeholder ad names. If there are inactive ads sitting in the account, they simply aren't visible in this particular file.
